committee.title: Committee Help
committee.definition: A Committee is a group or forum entrusted with certain responsibilities or decision making duties.

policy.title: Policy Help
policy.definition: A Policy describes the agreed manner in which an organisation should act in certain situations, e.g. to meet the needs of regulatory imperatives.

tips.breakdownRules: Policies can be broken down into rule sets to capture a more granular view.
tips.linkDependencies: Policies can be linked to other Policies to document dependencies.

process.title: Process Help
process.definition: A Process describes a set of manual or automated activities required to achieve a given outcome.

tips.predecessorFlow: Use edit mode and the process predecessor field to link process steps together and describe process flow.
tips.linkContext: Link Processes to Glossary and System items to describe their data and system context.

project.title: Project Help
project.definition: A Project describes a change effort (big or small) outside of Business As Usual activities.

tips.linkResources: Link Projects to the data, system and business resources they are looking to affect or rely on.
tips.breakdownSubprojects: Projects can be broken down into sub-projects to capture a more granular view.
tips.linkDependencies: Projects can be linked to other Projects to document dependencies.

dataset.title: Data Set Help
dataset.definition: Data sets commonly describe tables of data that reside in systems. Data sets are also used to describe reports, value lists, records or any other data structures.

tips.createSystemGlossaryFirst: Make sure System and Glossary objects are created first.
tips.attributesAddedHere: Attributes and attribute flows are added here.
tips.bulkUploader: When adding lots of Data Sets / Attributes, consider using the Bulk-Uploader.

system.title: System Help
system.definition: A System is a container of data, either in the traditional sense of a IT supported software application or a more tactical user application like Ms Excel, Ms Access etc.

tips.endUserComputing: Systems can be used to describe Ms Excel, Sharepoints, and other end user computing.

systemInterface.title: System Interface Help
systemInterface.definition: A system interface represents the flow of information between systems. After you create an interface, you can specify the flow of attributes through the interface.

tips.oneWay: Interfaces flow one way. To represent information moving in two directions, create two Interfaces.
tips.relatedSystemsDotted: When you create an interface, the related systems are represented as dotted lines in Maps.
tips.attributeFlows: Attribute level flows can be linked to interfaces (in Data Sets)

glossary.title: Glossary Help
glossary.definition: The Glossary captures an organisation's agreed definitions for different concepts, allowing for the creation of a common language.

tips.linkDataToBusiness: Glossary is how BUDG links data to the business viewpoints (e.g. process). A well populated glossary is essential for understanding and connecting data to its business context.
tips.structuredHierarchically: Glossary items can be structured hierarchically and be related to one another.

regulation.title: Regulation Help
regulation.definition: Regulation holds the organisation's interpretation of regulatory documentation

tips.linkExternalToInternal: BUDG can help you to link external regulation to internal policies to ensure compliance.

regulatoryTheme.title: Regulatory Theme Help
regulatoryTheme.definition: A regulatory theme classifies a regulation based on the type of legislation.

tips.classifyRegulations: This is used to classify regulations that have been created in BUDG, such as privacy and capital adequacy. The facet is hierarchical and allows grouping of themes.

regulator.title: Regulator Help
regulator.definition: A regulator is typically an official body that publishes or enforces a regulation.

tips.linkToRegulations: Enter the name of the regulatory body. After you create a regulator, you can link it to the regulations that it publishes or controls.

geography.title: Geography Help
geography.definition: Geography describes geographical regions or countries that are relevant to the aims of your data governance requirements.

tips.identifyCountries: Geography can be used to identify the countries that are affected by different regulations. Use the facet to show that a regulation applies only to certain countries or regions. The administrator must create one overall structure of geography to suit the needs of the whole BUDG instance. The facet is hierarchical. For example, countries such as France, Germany, and Spain can be grouped under Europe or Western Europe for easy group searches.

businessArea.title: Business Help
businessArea.definition: A Business Area is a department or team with certain assigned responsibilities within the wider organisation.

tips.notOrgUnit: Business Areas should not be confused with Org Units. Org Units contain the offical structure from an HR perspective whereas Business Areas are typically more fluid and in line with how the business is run.

capability.title: Capability Help
capability.definition: A Capability describes an organisational-level skill that is realised through people, process, and/or technology.

tips.topLevelView: Capabilities provide a top level view on how the firms data, IT assets and business resources interlink to make up organizational capabilities.
tips.linkCommittees: Capabilities can be linked to Committees to capture the corporate governance arrangements.

client.title: Client Help
client.definition: The Client inventory allows you to capture client segmentations and link those to the data, system and business resources that supports those client segments.

tips.topLevelView: Client segments provide a top level view on how the firm's data, IT assets and business resources support given Client segments.

legalEntity.title: Legal Entity Help
legalEntity.definition: Legal Entity describes the legal structure of the firm and / or its partners.

tips.linkAssets: Link Legal Entities to the data, system and business assets they rely on to capture their relevance from a Legal Entity perspective.

orgUnit.title: Org Unit Help
orgUnit.definition: Org Unit represents HR's view of the organisation's structure.

tips.integrateHr: BUDG can integrate with the firm's HR systems to source and refresh Org Unit information.

people.title: People Help
people.definition: The People inventory holds a list of the people in the organisation.

tips.assignRoles: Once created, People can be assigned different roles and responsibilities against each of the objects in BUDG.
tips.singleSignOn: BUDG can integrate with the firm's HR and autentication systems to support single sign-on.

product.title: Product Help
product.definition: The Product inventory allows you to capture Product segmentations and link those to the data, system and business resources that supports those client segments.

tips.topLevelView: Product segments provide a top level view on how the firm's data, IT assets and business resources support given Product segments.
